title: Hainanese Chicken Rice
subtitle: Poached chicken with fragrant rice cooked in chicken stock
excerpt: Hainanese chicken rice is the national dish of Singapore. The chicken is poached gently so it stays silky throughout, and the rice is cooked in the poaching stock to absorb all of that flavour.
sourceNotes: Brought to Singapore by Hainanese immigrants in the 19th century, this dish has become a cornerstone of Singaporean hawker culture.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The poaching stock can be made a day ahead. Store in the fridge and reheat before cooking the rice.

content.text: The most important thing is to never boil the chicken hard. A bare simmer keeps the flesh moist and tender throughout.
Put the chicken legs, ginger, spring onion, and garlic in the stockpot. Cover with 1.5 litres of cold water. Add a generous pinch of salt.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Skim off any foam from the surface. Reduce to the lowest possible simmer and cook for 40 minutes.
Remove the chicken and set aside to rest. Pour the stock through a sieve and reserve 600ml for cooking the rice.
Cook the rinsed rice with the 600ml of reserved stock in a rice cooker or in the stockpot with the lid on over low heat for 15 to 18 minutes until tender.
Remove the chicken skin if preferred, then slice or shred the meat from the bone.
Serve the chicken over bowls of rice. Drizzle with sesame oil and light soy. Add sliced cucumber alongside. Sprinkle with chilli flakes if using.

items.symptom: The chicken is rubbery and dry.
items.cause: The water boiled vigorously instead of simmering gently.
items.fix: Keep heat at lowest setting; only small bubbles should appear.

items.cause: Too little stock was used or the stock was diluted.
items.fix: Reduce the reserved stock a little before cooking the rice.

items.symptom: The rice is sticky and clumped.
items.cause: Too much water or the rice was not rinsed.
items.fix: Rinse rice until the water runs clear before cooking.
